rules.title: Non-move closure captures register field-path (RFC-2229) borrows
rules.statement: A non-`move` closure capturing place `p` by reference registers a borrow of `p` held for the closure holder's lifetime: a mutated/`&mut` capture registers a `&mut` (exclusive) loan, a shared capture registers a `&` (shared) loan/liveness check. A capture of a strict sub-field `p.x` registers a precise FIELD-PATH borrow (so disjoint sibling access `&mut p.y` beside `|| p.x` is allowed; a conflicting `&mut p.x` is rejected); a whole-root capture instead registers a whole-value borrow (mut) or a bare liveness check (shared), since Logos captures a whole variable and a whole-var shared borrow would otherwise block disjoint sibling mutation. Loans release at the closure holder's last use (NLL).
rules.divergence: RFC-2229 disjoint closure capture: field-path precision, but a whole-var SHARED capture is a liveness check only (not a recorded shared borrow) to avoid blocking sibling mutation

rules.title: move closure captures take ownership, registering no borrow
rules.statement: A `move` closure takes ownership of each captured place; it registers no borrow (the captured value is consumed into the closure rather than loaned).

rules.title: Borrows inside an aggregate literal are held by the binding the aggregate flows into
rules.statement: A `&`/`&mut` borrow placed into a struct/tuple/array LITERAL field or element is registered with the SAME holder that the aggregate value flows into (recursive borrow-taking), held for that holder's lifetime and released at the holder's last use (NLL), rather than only through the end of the constructing statement. Non-borrow fields/elements are consumed (move-tracked) as ordinary values. A `let` binding whose RHS is such an aggregate literal is routed the same way even when the binding's nominal type is not itself borrow-carrying.

rules.title: Borrows are non-lexical: released once the holder's last use has passed
rules.statement: A pre-pass over each fn body (`scan_uses_expr`/`scan_uses_stmt`/`scan_uses_block`) computes, per named local, the maximum line at which it is read. After visiting each statement in a block, every active borrow (whole-value or field-path) whose holder's last-use line is at or before the current statement's line is released (its exclusive-borrow flag cleared or shared-borrow count decremented). Borrows with no named holder are never released by this mechanism.

rules.title: Loop bodies: borrows are body-scoped, only moves of outer vars propagate
rules.statement: A loop body is analyzed in its own scope (loop-iteration variables declared local to it); borrows taken inside are released when the scope is popped at body end. Only MOVES of pre-existing OUTER variables propagate out of the loop to the enclosing state. Provenance is merged conservatively across the loop (the body may execute zero or more times).

rules.title: A let-bound reference borrowing into a per-statement temporary is rejected (E0716)
rules.statement: Binding a reference (or borrow-carrying value) whose provenance is a temporary value dropped at the end of the binding statement is an error: the reference would outlive its own statement, but the temporary it borrows into is dropped when the statement ends. The owning value must first be bound to a variable so it outlives the borrow.
examples: let h = make(); let v = h.view();  // ok
rules.divergence: Rust E0716 analog (temporary value dropped while borrowed)

rules.title: let RHS that is a reference / closure / borrow-carrying value / aggregate literal records a loan held by the binding
rules.statement: When a `let name = val;` has a value that is a reference kind, a closure type, a borrow-carrying-typed value (e.g. `v.iter_mut()`), or an aggregate literal (struct/tuple/array) that may itself hold nested borrows, the borrows reachable from `val` are recorded as loans held by `name` (released at `name`'s last use, NLL). Otherwise the value is visited as an ordinary consuming move (preserving move-tracking, e.g. `let h2 = h;`).

rules.title: Provenance flows from RHS to a let binding of reference, borrow-carrying, or lifetime-parameterized struct type
rules.statement: A `let` binding whose declared type is a reference or borrow-carrying type inherits the RHS's reference-provenance (`prov_of(val)`) into `prov_[name]`. A binding of a `struct`/`ZonedStruct` type that carries non-empty lifetime arguments also inherits the RHS provenance (the struct instance borrows through its lifetime parameter), feeding downstream dropck/outlives checks.

rules.title: Dropck-relevant let bindings record the local places they borrow from
rules.statement: When a `let` binds a value whose type is Drop-and-lifetime (dropck) relevant, the local variables the value borrows from are collected and recorded against the binding name (with its line), so that drop-order checking can detect a borrowed referent being dropped before the borrowing binding.

rules.title: Every binding records its borrow sources for end-of-scope outlives checking (E0597)
rules.statement: Every `let` binding (not only dropck-relevant ones) records the local borrow sources of its RHS value, so that at scope-pop a stored borrow whose holder outlives the referent it borrows from can be detected and rejected.
rules.divergence: Rust E0597 analog (borrowed value does not live long enough)
